text:
Petrov and Macdonald’s RecSys 2022 paper proposes Recency-based Sampling of Sequences (RSS): sample c=max(1,floor(τn)) target positions with replacement using p(k) ∝ α^(n−k), remove sampled items, and predict the resulting target set from the remaining ordered sequence. This is multiple-target removal, not prefix truncation: interactions after a sampled target can remain visible. α=1 gives uniform target sampling; α→0 concentrates sampling on the final item. Experiments apply RSS to GRU4Rec, Caser and SASRec; BERT4Rec is a comparator, not an RSS-trained architecture. [Paper, §4](https://arxiv.org/html/2207.02643#S4)

The α ablation finds uniform sampling substantially weaker, while intermediate recency weighting generally helps. Separately, the paper explicitly notes that BERT4Rec already includes some training examples with only the last item masked. Thus neither recency-weighted targets nor terminal masking alone establishes originality. [Paper, §§3.1, 6.3](https://arxiv.org/html/2207.02643)

Assessment: if the proposal samples one endpoint, discards its suffix, and predicts a terminal mask using BERT4Rec, its technical distinction from RSS includes strict prefix-only conditioning, a single positional target, and retained mask-position supervision—not merely a fixed endpoint probability. However, the proposal’s exact distribution/code was not supplied, so novelty remains conditional. Useful ablations: uniform versus recency-weighted prefix endpoints; endpoint-probability sweep; terminal-only versus mixed internal masking, holding backbone and training budget fixed.
